summary: AE + SE walked Orion Retail through the Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Key topics: per-route latency/cost, KV cache and batching, dedicated capacity benefits, data residency and SOC2, pilot scope and next steps. Customer asked about VPC/on-prem options and how rollouts/fallbacks work. Agreed to share pricing, benchmarks, and schedule a pilot kickoff.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Orion Head of ML), Samir Patel (Orion CTO), Hannah Kim (Orion DevOps), Tom Reyes (Product)
Shared docs/links: deck: https://redwood.example/sales/deck/orion-console-walkthrough, benchmark sheet: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/orion-sample, security packet link: https://redwood.example/security/orion-packet

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Daniel, our solutions engineer. We're gonna run through the Redwood console — usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and how you can see cost broken down by model and route. Any quick intros from Orion?

[00:18] Lena: Hi, yeah I'm Lena. Head of ML. We're evaluating serving options for our in-store assistant and recco engines. Samir, Hannah on the call too.

[00:28] Samir: Samir, CTO. We're mostly concerned about predictable costs and data residency.

[00:32] Daniel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: show the high-level analytics page, then per-route dashboards, then the cost/latency breakdown and how Optimize recommendations can be applied. We'll demo a couple of filters and then leave time for Q&A.

[00:45] Maya: Quick note — some of the transcript text may show weird names for products, ignore typos. We also shared the deck and benchmark sheet in the chat.

[01:05] Daniel: Alright jumping in — here's the Console home. You get a top-line usage chart: tokens in, tokens out, request count, and average latency. The chart's aggregated by day by default, and you can zoom in to hourly. (screen share)

[01:30] Lena: That looks useful. Can you show per-route? We have about 12 API routes — search, chat, summarization, receipts parsing.

[01:40] Daniel: Yep. Navigating to Routes, here's the per-route list. Each row shows request rate,  p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and error rate. You can click into a specific route — I'm gonna open 'in_store_assist_v2'.

[01:59] Maya: Note that the per-route view respects tags and environment filters, so you can split prod vs staging easily.

[02:10] [02:10] Tom: Sorry, the screen is a bit fuzzy on my end, but I can see columns. That cost per 1k tokens number — is that derived from your hosted pricing?

[02:20] Daniel: Good question. The console shows unit economics based on your selected configuration. If you use Hosted, it uses hosted per-token rates; if you're on Dedicated, it maps the pool throughput and amortized GPU costs to a per-token estimate. That's in the Cost Breakdown panel.

[02:40] Lena: How accurate are Dedicated estimates? We wanna know if reserved capacity will actually lower unit costs for our high-throughput routes.

[02:48] Daniel: For Dedicated we use measured throughput from similar workloads and our kernel profiles. We show two columns: model-run cost (GPU hours amortized) and infra overhead (networking, cache RAM). For your profile, we can provide a sample amortization in the benchmark sheet — that's what I'll attach after this.

[03:05] Samir: Do you include batching and KV cache effects in the estimate? Those can swing numbers a lot for us.

[03:12] Daniel: Yes, there's a separate Optimization assumptions section. We simulate continuous batching and prefix cache hit-rate. In the routes panel you can toggle cache hit-rate (0-100%) and see cost/latency update live — this is helpful for recco routes vs conversational ones.

[03:32] [03:32] Hannah: Quick perf question: our maximum payload is 8k tokens for receipts, average 700 tokens. How does sequence length distribution factor in kernel selection?

[03:42] Daniel: The runtime collects seq length histograms and picks kernels accordingly; the Console shows the distribution and the model kernel profile it expects. If you have long-tail 8k requests we can recommend longer-context model variants or quantization changes.

[04:05] Maya: Let's demo a cost drill-down. I'm going to click Costs -> By Model -> filter to the last 30 days.

[04:15] Daniel: Here you can see per-model token volume, token-type (prompt vs completion), and effective $/1k tokens. There's also an option to attribute costs back to routes, teams, or even customer ids via tags.

[04:32] Lena: Attribution to teams is big for us. We bill internal teams. How are tags applied?

[04:38] Daniel: We support tagging at the request level via header or SDK. You can enforce tag schemas with route policies. The Console's Cost Allocation view lets you define tag-based allocation rules and export CSVs for chargeback.

[04:58] Samir: On security — we need audit logs and KMS integration if we do Private deployments. Does the Console show KMS usage and key rotations?

[05:08] Maya: Yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Audit logs surface key usage events and console actions. We also provide an events-exporter for SIEM ingestion. Security packet link is in the chat.

[05:25] [05:25] Tom: Can you show the per-request trace? We want to see where latency spikes happen — is it model startup, network, or batching delays?

[05:33] Daniel: Sure — open a single route, click a request sample — here's a flame-graph like trace: client -> gateway -> batcher -> model run -> kv-cache lookup -> response. You can see p50/p95 per segment. For cold-starts there's a separate indicator when a model was pulled into memory.

[05:58] Hannah: The KV cache shows as 'K V cash' in the docs sometimes — I've seen transcription errors earlier in our notes. Just making sure that's KV cache.

[06:05] Daniel: (laughs) yes, KV cache. Some of our auto transcriptions are weird.

[06:12] [06:12] Maya: Next I'm going to show the Optimize tab. This is where we put suggestions: batching window sizes, suggested quantization profile for a model, and recommended autoscaler settings. You can accept suggestions and apply them to a dev route.

[06:30] Lena: How invasive is quantization? We worry about quality regressions on our NLU.

[06:36] Daniel: Good call. Optimize includes a quality-guard: it runs a baseline eval against your provided prompt set and flags regressions by percentage. You can choose conservative quant profiles first, e.g., 8-bit dynamic vs more aggressive 4-bit. Those recommendations are versioned and tied to rollout policies.

[06:55] Samir: About rollouts: we want canary then auto-fallback to a previous model variant if anomalies happen. Does Redwood support that?

[07:03] Maya: Yes, we have rollouts in Console. You can configure canary percentage, time window, and automatic rollback if latency or quality thresholds breach. Also route-level fallback policies — if Dedicated pool is saturated we can route to Hosted or a smaller model variant.

[07:22] Daniel: I'm going to simulate a canary. (click) Setting canary to 10% for 30 minutes. Console shows projected cost delta and expectedLatency chart.

[07:38] Tom: If the canary fails, will logs and diffs be exposed for quick triage?

[07:43] Daniel: Yes, the rollout UI links to diffs, per-request examples where outputs diverged, and the eval set results. You can annotate and mark as reviewed.

[07:58] [07:58] Maya: Let's talk about the cost model again. For your traffic profile, we've run a sample with 3 main routes: search (high QPS, short responses), chat (medium QPS, longer responses), summarization (low QPS, long responses). I'll open the cost breakdown for last 7 days.

[08:18] Daniel: Here is a stacked bar: charges broken into model compute, infra overhead, caching savings, and storage. Notice caching saved about 27% on search. That updates live when we change cache hit-rate parameter.

[08:34] Lena: 27% is significant. What assumptions went into cache hit-rate?

[08:40] Daniel: Default is measured hits on prefix reuse for search (we infer prefix reuse from similar requests) but you can plug in your own observed hit-rate. The Console will recompute savings.

[08:55] Hannah: For Dedicated, can we reserve GPUs only for certain routes? We don't want to reserve for low-priority batch jobs.

[09:02] Maya: Yes, Dedicated pools can be tagged and routes pinned to pools. You can also configure burst to hosted for overflow. We showed an example of pinning 'in_store_assist' to Pool-A and allowing 'summarize_backfill' to run on shared pools.

[09:22] Samir: If we do Dedicated, what's SLA on latency?

[09:27] Maya: With Dedicated we offer an SLA-backed latency target depending on pool size and commit tier. We'll include exact numbers in the pricing doc.

[09:35] [09:35] Daniel: I want to show a feature — model variant substitution. If a requested model isn't available in the pool, you can configure an automatic compatible variant fallback. The Console surfaces compatibility and expected delta on quality/cost.

[09:53] Tom: Do you have examples of customers who moved to Dedicated and saw cost savings?

[09:59] Maya: We do. We'll include anonymized case studies in the follow-up — typical wins are for sustained high QPS text-generation workloads.

[10:10] [10:10] Lena: On data residency: we operate across EU and NA regions. We need logs and model activations to stay in EU for EU customers. How is that enforced?

[10:18] Daniel: The Console has region-aware routing and you can pin routes to regions. For Private deployments we can ensure control plane sits in your VPC in the EU. We also support audit exports that only contain EU-hosted events.

[10:35] Hannah: For a pilot, how much setup is needed to get per-route analytics? We want to demo cost allocation quickly.

[10:42] Daniel: Minimal — instrument the SDK or headers with route and team tags, point traffic at a dev account, and the Console will auto-populate routes. We can seed sample tags and demo in <24 hours with a test token.

[10:58] Maya: I'll create a demo account for you and share credentials. Daniel will put a sample traffic profile in the benchmark sheet so you can see the modeled savings.

[11:12] [11:12] Samir: A couple security Qs — SSO/SAML? RBAC? We need granular controls for routes.

[11:18] Maya: We support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. You can limit access to cost views or rollout controls per role. All described in the security packet link.

[11:32] Lena: If we want on-prem, is there an offline upgrade path? We have some air-gapped environments.

[11:38] Daniel: We offer an on-prem package. Control plane can be hybrid — some customers run the control plane in their VPC and model infra on-prem. Air-gapped installs are a heavier lift; we have an engineering engagement for that.

[11:55] [11:55] Tom: Can the Console export a CSV with per-request charges for our billing team?

[12:01] Daniel: Yes — Cost Allocation -> Export. You can configure granularity down to request-level, include tags, timestamps, and model details. Exports are S3-compatible or direct CSV download.

[12:15] Maya: Let's step through a scenario: Say in-store assistant spikes 3x during Black Friday. How do we prevent cost blowouts while preserving SLA?

[12:25] Daniel: You can set route quotas and rate limits, apply cheaper model fallbacks, enable caching aggressively, and prioritize routes on Dedicated pools. Console will simulate projected costs under your spike profile — we can run a what-if with your traffic.

[12:42] Lena: If we throttle, we don't want to kill critical flows. Is it possible to set tiered throttles?

[12:47] Daniel: Yes — priority queues and per-route throttles, plus a preemption policy for business-critical routes.

[12:55] [12:55] Hannah: On metrics retention: how long do you keep per-request traces? We have compliance that requires 90 days of traces but not full payloads.

[13:03] Maya: You can set retention policies. We store traces and metadata for configurable retention and can redact payloads to meet privacy needs.

[13:18] Daniel: Back to the Console UI — I'm gonna create a saved report: 'March Cost by Team' and show how to schedule weekly email exports. (click)

[13:30] Tom: Nice. Can that report include projected savings if we enable caching and switch this route to Dedicated?

[13:36] Daniel: Yes, you can toggle the assumptions in the report and the projection updates.

[13:45] [13:45] Maya: Quick check — any blockers for pilot?

[13:50] Lena: We need to confirm compliance requirements and the internal billing owner. Also want to see an end-to-end pilot plan.

[13:58] Maya: Sounds good. We'll suggest a pilot plan (2-4 weeks) focusing on search and chat routes, run benchmarks, and instrument Optimize recommendations.

[14:10] [14:10] Samir: Operational question — who will own the pilot? We have limited SRE capacity.

[14:15] Maya: Our solutions team will help with onboarding. There's a light-touch self-serve flow but for pilot we'll assign an SE (Daniel) to assist.

[14:25] Hannah: Do you have a standard SLA for pilot environments?

[14:29] Daniel: Pilot accounts are best-effort but we can provide a pre-prod dedicated pool for the pilot if you commit to a short reserved window. We'll include options in pricing.

[14:42] [14:42] Lena: Let's cover billing — is there a minimum commit for Dedicated?

[14:48] Maya: Yes, Dedicated has monthly/annual commit tiers. We'll share the pricing sheet; the math in the Console can be mapped to commit tiers.

[14:58] Daniel: Small demo: toggling cache hit-rate for search from 30% to 60% — watch cost drop and latency improve. (click) You can also pin that change to a staging route to validate.

[15:18] Tom: If we accept an Optimize recommendation, is the change applied automatically to prod?

[15:23] Daniel: By default it applies to dev/staging. You must explicitly approve for prod. We also support a sweep where you can auto-apply conservative optimizations but require manual approval for aggressive ones.

[15:38] [15:38] Samir: Any special considerations for HIPAA/health data? Not our primary but might touch PII in receipts.

[15:45] Maya: We have HIPAA-compliant controls in Private deployments and appropriate BAAs. We'll include the HIPAA section in the security packet.

[15:58] Daniel: I'm going to pull up the benchmark sheet we referenced. Here are sample numbers for a retail search workload: tokens/sec metrics, amortized GPU cost per 1M tokens, and caching savings. I'll drop this to the shared link.

[16:12] [16:12] Lena: For model family, do you support half-precision and mixed-precision kernels? We've got mixed hardware in-house.

[16:19] Daniel: Yes — kernel selection handles fp16, int8, and mixed kernels. The Console will flag incompatible hw-model combos.

[16:34] Hannah: How do I get the console demo account you mentioned?

[16:38] Maya: I'll create the dev tenant and send creds after the call. Daniel will add seeded routes and a sample traffic profile.

[16:48] [16:48] Tom: Process question: what approvals do you need from us to start pilot?

[16:52] Maya: Signature on an SOW for the pilot (simple), access to a test dataset and the traffic profile, and a kickoff meeting with your ops and security. We'll draft a one-page SOW.

[17:05] Samir: Can we get a price estimate for a 3-month pilot including a small dedicated pool?

[17:09] Maya: Yes, we'll include that in the pricing doc. We'll give a low, mid, high bucket based on throughput.

[17:16] [17:16] Daniel: Quick demo endcap — the Console has a change history so you can audit who changed a rollout or applied an Optimize suggestion.

[17:26] Lena: That's helpful.

[17:30] Maya: Any final questions?

[17:35] Tom: I'm good, just want the demo account and pricing.

[17:38] Hannah: Same, please include our retention and KMS requirements in the packet.

[17:42] Samir: We'll send the traffic profile and tag schema.

[17:45] Maya: Great — recap of next steps: Maya sends pricing + SOW + demo tenant; Daniel sends benchmark sheet + seeded routes; Orion to send traffic profile and compliance list. We'll aim to have pilot scope doc by next week.

[17:59] [17:59] Lena: Thanks all. Looking forward to the pilot.

[18:02] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (K V cash, Redwood Dedicated spelled odd). Some timestamps approximate; actual call ran 48 minutes.
